subject: literature
passage: Anton Chekhov's story "The Lady with the Dog" (1899) begins with Dmitri Gurov, a jaded Moscow banker who regards women with contempt, starting an affair at a seaside resort that he expects to forget within weeks. Instead, back in Moscow, he cannot stop thinking of Anna, and by the end he recognizes that only now, as his hair turns gray, has he truly fallen in love. Critic Elif Arslan reads the story as a tale of redemption: love has transformed a cynic into a man capable of tenderness.
passage_b: Gurov's change of heart is genuine; Chekhov leaves no doubt that he has come to love Anna. What the story withholds is any sense that this love has delivered him. Its final scene finds the lovers in a Moscow hotel room, still meeting in secret, still married to others, and still unable to imagine how they might live openly. They feel that a solution must be near, yet both understand that the hardest part has barely begun. A reading that ends in redemption completes a story that Chekhov deliberately leaves open.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the reading of the story in Text 1?

choices.A: By denying that Gurov comes to feel genuine love for Anna by the end of the story
choices.B: By granting that Gurov changes but denying that the story resolves his situation
choices.C: By claiming that the lovers find a way to live together openly in the story's final scene
choices.D: By suggesting that the story's open ending reveals Chekhov's disapproval of the affair

explanation.why: Text 2 agrees that "Gurov's change of heart is genuine," accepting part of Arslan's reading. It objects that the story "withholds any sense that this love has delivered him": the lovers are still hiding, and "the hardest part has barely begun." A redemption reading, Text 2 says, "completes a story that Chekhov deliberately leaves open."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says Chekhov "leaves no doubt that he has come to love Anna."
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 accepts that Gurov truly changes but says calling it redemption imposes an ending that the open final scene withholds.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says the lovers are "still unable to imagine how they might live openly."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says the ending is open, but it never says Chekhov disapproves of the affair.
